text:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can we get a concrete preflight summary for kernel v3? Specifically: rollout timing, any default batching changes, and caching/ejection semantics?

sasha: Short answer: targeting rollout next sprint (~2 weeks). No forced defaults for hosted customers; most changes are opt-in during canary. More below.

devon: Adding infra details: v3 ships dynamic attention kernels + some quantization-safe paths. Staged canary plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100%. We'll monitor latency, error-rate, and eval scores.

ajay: From product side: no API surface change. We'll update SKUs and docs. Customers on Dedicated can request early access.

maria: Any rough perf deltas we can share now (8k / 32k contexts)?

devon: Early internal runs: median p95 token latency down ~18% at 8k, ~25% at 32k on a8g; throughput +12% for steady streams. Model-dependent. We'll publish a benchmark dashboard next week.

zane: Does this change prefix caching or KV eviction? We're worried about cache invalidations increasing token cost.

devon: No API-level changes. Default eviction TTL stays 60s. We're surfacing a new LRU+weight eviction behind a flag for canary users. If teams want in, DM me.

sasha: Risk notes: main risk is quantization regression on a subset of models. Research will run prompt-set evals continuously; if end-to-end quality drops >1.5% we auto-pause rollout.

maria: Action items + owners?

ajay: Product will publish a one-pager with timeline, affected SKUs, and migration notes by EOD Friday.

devon: Infra will open a canary runbook with rollback steps and alert thresholds. Runbook link: https://intra.redwood/ops/canary-kernel-v3

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: kernel-v3-canary at 1956010000 :spiral_calendar: (automated note)

sasha: We'll host office hours next Thurs 3pm PT to walk teams through changes and take live questions.

maria: Thanks. pinging @devon to add our "maria-team" workload to canary.

devon: Done — added "maria-team" to canary list. I'll DM you access to logs and the perf dashboard.

zane: One small ask: will default batching window increase? Small-req latency was a concern in the demo.

devon: Default batching window remains 10ms. Experiments may test 15ms behind opt-in only. We'll include cost/latency tradeoffs in the dashboard so teams can decide.

maria: Awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
